Guide

A holiday home in Tuscany with your dog

At Casa La Fonte up to two dogs are very welcome. The whole property is yours, the lanes around the village are quiet, and the hills start at the door. Here is what to know before you come.

By Daniel & Eva, owners of Casa La Fonte

At the house

You have the main house, the guesthouse, the terraces, the lawn and the pool to yourselves; no one else stays on the property. The pet fee is €75 per stay, whatever the length; just add your dog in the request form and tell us a little about them. Please note that the garden is not fenced and there is a steep drop behind the lawn, so keep an eye on your dog there.

Walks from the door

Trails start in the village and lead up to the Rocca Sillana fortress and through oak woods and fields. Traffic on the lanes is light. In summer, walk early in the morning and in the evening, and keep the middle of the day for the shade of the loggia.

Beaches with dogs

The Etruscan Coast is 45 to 60 minutes away. Cecina and San Vincenzo have stretches of beach and beach clubs that accept dogs. In Tuscany dogs are allowed on a lead in public outdoor areas, including beaches, subject to local rules, which can change by season, so check before you go. Bring water and shade.

Eating out

Many trattorias in the area are happy to have a well-behaved dog on the terrace. It is always polite to ask first.

Before you travel

  • Within the EU your dog needs a pet passport and a valid rabies vaccination.
  • Bring your dog's bed and bowls; we'll tell you where the nearest vet is when you book.
  • July and August are hot: plan outings for the cooler hours. The thick stone walls keep the house pleasant.

Driving times are approximate, from the house in San Dalmazio.

Stay with us

Casa La Fonte is a 400-year-old stone farmhouse with a guesthouse and a private heated saltwater pool in San Dalmazio, for up to seven guests. Dogs are welcome.
